info.name: CourseWave API
info.description:
# CourseWave API

REST API for **CourseWave**, a subscription-based learning platform: one subscription unlocks every instructor's courses, and every payment is shared with the instructors a student actually learns from.

This collection covers every endpoint the Next.js student app uses, in the order a student meets them.

## Quick start
1. Import this collection. It already points at `http://localhost:8000`, so **no environment file is needed**. To use another server, change the `base_url` collection variable (Collection → Variables → Current value).
2. Send **1. Authentication → Login**. Its test script stores the bearer token in the `token` variable.
3. Send **2. Catalog → List published courses**. It stores `course_slug`.
4. Folders **4** and most of **5** need an **active subscription**. Either pay in Stripe test mode (**3. → Initiate checkout**, open the returned URL, pay with `4242 4242 4242 4242`, then **Confirm subscription**) or log in as a seeded demo student (table below).
5. Run a whole folder with the **Collection Runner**; requests chain through the variables.

## Legend
| Badge | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 🌐 | Public, no token |
| 🔑 | Any signed-in user |
| 💳 | Signed in **and** an active subscription |
| 🧪 | Local/demo only; returns 404 in production |

## Conventions
- **Base URL:** `{{base_url}}` is a collection variable (default `http://localhost:8000`). All API routes live under `/api`.
- **Auth:** `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}` (Laravel Sanctum). It is set once on the collection; public requests override it with *No Auth*.
- **Always send `Accept: application/json`** (every request here does). Without it Laravel may answer a failed auth with a redirect instead of a 401.
- **Envelope:** every JSON response is `{ "success": bool, "message": string, "data": any, "errors": object|null }`.
- **Money** is always integer cents (`*_cents`); `*_human` fields are display strings.
- **Dates** are ISO 8601; `*_human` fields are relative text computed when the response is built.
- **Pagination:** `?page=N`, with `meta.current_page`, `meta.last_page`, `meta.total`.

## Status codes
| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 / 201 | Success / created |
| 401 | Missing or invalid token |
| 403 | No active subscription, or not allowed |
| 404 | Not found (also used for records that belong to someone else) |
| 409 | Certificate PDF is still being generated |
| 422 | Validation failed; see `errors` |
| 429 | Rate limited (comment posting/editing: 20 per minute; certificate verification: 30 per minute) |

## Test accounts
Created by the demo setup (`.\scripts\setup.ps1 -Mode demo`). Change the `login_email` / `login_password` collection variables to switch.
| Account | Password | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `student@llm.com` | `student@12334` | Student without a subscription |
| `instructor@llm.com` | `instructor@12334` | Can reply to comments on their own lessons |
| `admin@llm.com` | `admin@12334` | Uses the Filament panel, not this API |
| `demo.student01@llm.com` … `demo.student26@llm.com` | `Password123` | Created by the demo setup (or `php artisan db:seed --class=AnalyticsDemoSeeder`). These have **active subscriptions** and learning history. |

Production has no default accounts: create the admin with `php artisan coursewave:create-admin`, and register students through the app.

Instructor and admin dashboards are Filament panels at `{{base_url}}/instructor` and `{{base_url}}/admin`; they are not part of this API.

## Realtime
Notifications are also pushed over Laravel Reverb (WebSocket, default port 8080) on the private channel `private-App.Models.User.{id}`. Folder 7 documents the REST side and the channel-auth call Laravel Echo makes.

## Server URL
`base_url` is a collection variable whose default (`http://localhost:8000`) matches the Docker setup. Point it at another server by editing its **Current value**. If you create a Postman environment of your own, define only `base_url` in it. **Do not add a `token` variable to an environment**: environment values override collection values, and an empty one would hide the token the Login script stores.

variable.description: API origin. Default matches the Docker setup; edit the Current value to target another server.
Sanctum bearer token. Set by Login/Register, cleared by Logout.
Account used by the Login request.
Password used by the Login request.
Signed-in user id. Set by Login / Me.
Set by Initiate checkout; used by Confirm subscription.
Set by Course learning tree (first lesson that has a quiz).
Set by My certificates. The default is a placeholder that returns 404.

item.name: 1. Authentication
item.description:
Create an account, sign in, and sign out.

Self-registration creates a **student** (an **instructor** is also allowed). **Admin accounts can never self-register**; create one with `php artisan coursewave:create-admin`.

Login returns a Sanctum personal access token. It stays valid until you log out.

request.description:
**Access:** 🌐 Public

Creates a student (or instructor) account. `role` accepts `student` or `instructor`; `admin` is always rejected.

The email uses `{{$timestamp}}` so you can send this repeatedly.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 201 | Account created (a token may be returned) |
| 422 | Validation failed, e.g. email taken, password too short or not confirmed |

exec: const token = data.token || data.access_token || data.plain_text_token || json.token;
pm.test('A bearer token was returned', () => pm.expect(token, 'token field in the response').to.be.a('string'));

request.description:
**Access:** 🌐 Public

Signs in and returns a bearer token. The test script saves it to `token` so every other request is authenticated automatically.

Change `login_email` / `login_password` (collection variables) to switch accounts; see the accounts table in the collection description.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Signed in; token returned |
| 422 | Wrong credentials or missing fields |

**Access:** 🔑 Signed in

Returns the authenticated user and their role. Also stores `user_id`, which the channel-auth request in folder 7 needs.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | The current user |
| 401 | Missing or invalid token. Run Login first |

**Access:** 🔑 Signed in

Revokes the current token. The test script clears the `token` variable.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Token revoked |
| 401 | Already signed out |

item.name: 2. Catalog (public)
item.description: Browse published courses. **No account needed**: this is what the landing page and the public course pages use.

exec: const list = Array.isArray(d) ? d : ((d && (d.items || d.data || d.courses)) || []);

query.description: Optional text to filter by title

request.description:
**Access:** 🌐 Public

Lists published courses (drafts are never shown). Stores the first course's slug in `course_slug` for the requests that follow.

Enable the `search` query parameter to filter by title.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Courses returned |

**Access:** 🌐 Public

Same endpoint as above with `search=laravel` filled in, as a ready-made example.

**Access:** 🌐 Public

Course details with its modules and lesson titles. Lesson **content** is not included: that needs a subscription (folder 4).

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Course returned |
| 404 | No published course with that slug |

item.name: 3. Plans & Subscriptions
item.description:
Plans are paid **up front** (monthly, 3-month, annual). Payment goes through Stripe Checkout; the Stripe **webhook** is the authoritative confirmation, and **Confirm subscription** is the idempotent fallback the app calls after the redirect.

**Cancelling** refunds the days that have not elapsed yet; days already used are never refunded.

To pay in test mode: run **Initiate checkout**, open the returned URL, pay with `4242 4242 4242 4242` (any future date, any CVC), then run **Confirm subscription**.

exec: const list = Array.isArray(d) ? d : ((d && (d.items || d.data || d.plans)) || []);

request.description:
**Access:** 🌐 Public

The plans a student can buy. Stores the first plan's id in `plan_id`.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Plans returned |

exec: if (url) { console.log('Open this URL and pay with a Stripe test card: ' + url); }

request.description:
**Access:** 🔑 Signed in

Creates a Stripe Checkout session for the chosen plan. The response contains the URL to open; the session id is stored in `stripe_session_id` (check the Postman Console for the URL).

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 / 201 | Checkout session created |
| 422 | Unknown or inactive plan |

**Access:** 🔑 Signed in

Activates the subscription after payment. **Idempotent**: safe to call repeatedly, and safe if the Stripe webhook already activated it first. Switching plans cancels the previous subscription and refunds its unused days.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Subscription is active |
| 422 | Payment not completed, or the session belongs to another account |

**Access:** 🔑 Signed in

The student's subscription history, newest first.

**Access:** 🔑 Signed in

The active subscription, or `null` when there is none. Includes `refundable_cents` / `refundable_human`: what cancelling right now would refund (unused days only).

**Access:** 🔑 Signed in

Cancels the active subscription, voids the days that have not elapsed yet, and queues a refund for exactly those days. Instructors are never charged back for days already used. Calling it again changes nothing.

⚠️ This ends your test subscription; re-run checkout to get one again.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Canceled (a refund is queued when there were unused days) |
| 404 / 422 | No active subscription |

item.name: 4. Learning
item.description:
Course content for subscribers. **Every request in this folder needs an active subscription**; without one the API answers **403**.

Run *Course learning tree* first: it stores `lesson_id` and `quiz_id` for the rest of the folder.

item.name: Course & lessons
item.description:
The course outline, lesson content, and progress tracking.

Progress drives both the course completion percentage and instructor payouts (engagement seconds decide how a subscription is split), so the API caps each heartbeat at 120 seconds.

request.description:
**Access:** 💳 Subscribed student

Modules and lessons with the student's status on each (`not_started`, `in_progress`, `completed`), plus `completion_percent`. Stores the first lesson as `lesson_id` and the first lesson with a quiz as `quiz_id`.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Course tree |
| 403 | No active subscription |
| 404 | Course not found or not published |

**Access:** 💳 Subscribed student

One lesson: video URL or reading body, resource links, the student's progress, and the previous/next lesson ids.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Lesson content |
| 403 | No active subscription |
| 404 | Lesson not found or its course isn't published |

**Access:** 💳 Subscribed student

What the video player sends every ~15 seconds: the seconds watched **since the last report**. Values above 120 are rejected.

Response `data`: `status`, `watched_seconds`, `certificate_issued`.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Recorded |
| 403 | No active subscription |
| 422 | `watched_seconds` out of range |

exec: if (json.data && json.data.certificate_issued) { console.log('This completion finished the course: a certificate was issued.'); }

request.description:
**Access:** 💳 Subscribed student

Marks the lesson complete (the "Mark as complete" button, or the end of a video). Completing the **last** lesson of a course issues the certificate; `certificate_issued` is `true` only on that one response.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Completed |
| 403 | No active subscription |

item.name: Quizzes
item.description: Quick quizzes attached to lessons. Correct answers are **never** sent before you submit, and grading is always done on the server.

request.description:
**Access:** 💳 Subscribed student

The questions and answer options (without which one is correct). Use the question and option ids here to fill the submit request.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Quiz |
| 403 | No active subscription |
| 404 | Quiz not found |

**Access:** 💳 Subscribed student

`answers` maps each **question id** to the chosen **option id**. Replace the sample ids with the ones from *Quiz detail*. The server grades it and returns the score; correct answers are revealed only now.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Graded |
| 403 | No active subscription |
| 422 | Missing or invalid answers |

**Access:** 💳 Subscribed student

The student's own past attempts on this quiz.

item.name: Live sessions
item.description:
Live Q&A sessions hosted by instructors.

The **join link is a server-side secret**: `join_url` is `null` until 15 minutes before the start and until then `can_join` is `false`. A link that is not `https://` is never sent.

exec: pm.test('No raw meeting_url is ever exposed', () => (json.data.items || []).forEach(s => pm.expect(s).to.not.have.property('meeting_url')));

request.description:
**Access:** 💳 Subscribed student

Upcoming and live sessions for the courses the student has **started** (at least one lesson opened). Canceled, ended and unpublished-course sessions never appear. Ordered by start time, up to 50.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Sessions |
| 403 | No active subscription |

response.name: 200 OK: one upcoming, one live
response.body:

request.description:
**Access:** 💳 Subscribed student

One course's upcoming and live sessions. Any subscriber can see these, even before starting the course, so sessions can be discovered first.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Sessions |
| 403 | No active subscription |
| 404 | Course not found or not published |

item.name: 5. Discussion
item.description:
Threaded comments on lessons. Threads are **two levels deep** (a comment and its replies). Bodies are plain text, up to 2000 characters.

Access is decided by a policy, not just by the subscription middleware: a **subscribed student**, the course's **instructor** (no subscription needed) or an **admin** can take part. Anyone else gets 403.

The instructor badge (`is_instructor`) is computed by the server and can't be faked from the client. Posting and editing are limited to **20 requests per minute**.

query.description: 10 top-level comments per page, newest first; each carries its replies (oldest first)

request.description:
**Access:** 💳 Subscribed student, course instructor, or admin

Top-level comments, 10 per page, newest first, each with its replies. A deleted comment that still has replies appears as a placeholder (`is_deleted: true`, no body, no author). Stores the first comment's id in `comment_id`.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Comments |
| 403 | Not allowed to join this discussion |
| 404 | Lesson's course isn't published |

response.name: 200 OK: a question with an instructor reply
response.body:
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Comments retrieved.",
  "data": {
    "items": [
      {
        "id": 12,
        "parent_id": null,
        "is_deleted": false,
        "body": "Could you explain this part again?",
        "author": { "id": 41, "name": "Amira Hassan", "avatar_url": null },
        "is_instructor": false,
        "is_mine": false,
        "can_edit": false,
        "can_delete": false,
        "edited": false,
        "created_at": "2026-11-08T14:22:10+02:00",
        "created_at_human": "1 day ago",
        "replies": [
          {
            "id": 13,
            "parent_id": 12,
            "is_deleted": false,
            "body": "Sure! Re-read the previous section, then run the example step by step.",
            "author": { "id": 2, "name": "Sarah Chen", "avatar_url": null },
            "is_instructor": true,
            "is_mine": false,
            "can_edit": false,
            "can_delete": false,
            "edited": false,
            "created_at": "2026-11-08T16:05:44+02:00",
            "created_at_human": "23 hours ago",
            "replies": []
          }
        ]
      }
    ],
    "meta": { "current_page": 1, "last_page": 1, "total": 1 }
  },
  "errors": null
}

response.name: 403 Forbidden: no active subscription

exec: pm.test('parent_id is null for a top-level comment', () => pm.expect(json.data.parent_id).to.equal(null));

request.description:
**Access:** 💳 Subscribed student, course instructor, or admin

Posts a top-level comment. `body` is required (1–2000 characters after trimming). Any `is_instructor` or `user_id` you send is ignored. Stores the new id in `comment_id`. Rate limit: 20 per minute.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 201 | Posted |
| 403 | Not allowed to join this discussion |
| 404 | Lesson's course isn't published |
| 422 | Empty or too-long body |
| 429 | Too many requests |

response.name: 422 Unprocessable: reply to a reply

exec: pm.test('The reply points at the parent comment', () => pm.expect(String(json.data.parent_id)).to.equal(String(pm.collectionVariables.get('comment_id'))));

request.description:
**Access:** 💳 Subscribed student, course instructor, or admin

Same endpoint as *Post a comment* with `parent_id` set. The parent must be a live, **top-level** comment on the **same lesson**. The parent's author is notified (never yourself), and so is the lesson's instructor.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 201 | Reply posted |
| 422 | Parent is itself a reply, belongs to another lesson, or was deleted |

**Access:** 🔑 The comment's **author only**

Not even the course instructor or an admin can edit someone else's words. The comment shows "edited" afterwards. Rate limit: 20 per minute.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Updated |
| 403 | Not your comment |
| 422 | Empty or too-long body |

**Access:** 🔑 The comment's author, the **course instructor**, or an **admin**

A soft delete. A top-level comment that still has replies stays in the thread as a "deleted" placeholder so the replies keep their context; one without replies disappears. Deleting twice returns 404.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Deleted |
| 403 | Not allowed to delete this comment |
| 404 | Already deleted or not found |

item.name: 6. Certificates
item.description:
A certificate is issued automatically when a student completes **every lesson** of a course (quizzes don't count). The PDF is generated in the background; if it isn't ready yet, download returns **409**.

A student keeps their certificates even after a subscription ends. **Verification is public**: anyone with the number can confirm it is genuine, and the response never includes an email address.

request.description:
**Access:** 🔑 Signed in

The student's own certificates, newest first. Stores the first one's id and number. No subscription is needed.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Certificates (possibly an empty list) |
| 401 | Not signed in |

response.name: 200 OK
response.body:
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Certificates retrieved.",
  "data": [
    {
      "id": 3,
      "certificate_number": "CW-7K3M-9QWD-XT4P",
      "course_title": "Laravel for Beginners",
      "course_slug": "laravel-for-beginners",
      "instructor_name": "Sarah Chen",
      "issued_at": "2026-11-05T11:30:00+02:00",
      "issued_at_human": "November 5, 2026",
      "pdf_ready": true,
      "verification_url": "http://localhost:3000/verify/CW-7K3M-9QWD-XT4P"
    }
  ],
  "errors": null
}

exec: pm.test('PDF delivered, or still being prepared', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 409]));

request.description:
**Access:** 🔑 The certificate's owner

Returns the PDF. In Postman use **Send and Download** to save the file. Someone else's certificate id looks exactly like a missing one.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | The PDF |
| 404 | Not found, or not yours |
| 409 | PDF still being generated; retry in a moment (the request re-queues it) |

exec: pm.test('Valid certificate, or a clean 404 for an unknown number', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 404]));
pm.test('Only public fields are exposed', () => { pm.expect(json.data.valid).to.be.true; pm.expect(json.data).to.not.have.property('email'); });

request.description:
**Access:** 🌐 Public (30 requests per minute)

Confirms a certificate by its number and returns only what is printed on it: student name, course, instructor, issue date. The number is forgiving: lowercase, spaces and missing hyphens are accepted.

Until you run *My certificates*, the default placeholder number returns 404.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Genuine certificate |
| 404 | No such certificate |
| 429 | Too many requests |

response.name: 200 OK: genuine certificate

item.name: 7. Notifications & Realtime
item.description:
Every notification is **stored** (so none are lost while you're offline) **and** pushed live over WebSocket. These endpoints serve the stored list that the bell in the app shows.

Any signed-in user has notifications: students, instructors and admins; no subscription is needed. You can only ever read or mark **your own**; another user's notification id looks like a missing one (404).

**Realtime:** Laravel Echo connects to Reverb (`ws://localhost:8080`) and subscribes to `private-App.Models.User.{id}`. The channel-auth call is the last request in this folder.

request.description:
**Access:** 🔑 Signed in

Your notifications, 15 per page, newest first, plus `unread_count`. Stores the first one's id in `notification_id`.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Notifications |
| 401 | Not signed in |

response.name: 200 OK

exec: pm.test('Only unread items returned', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); (json.data.items || []).forEach(n => pm.expect(n.is_read).to.be.false); });

request.description:
**Access:** 🔑 Signed in

Same endpoint filtered with `unread=1`.

**Access:** 🔑 Signed in

Just the number for the bell badge (the app polls this every 60 seconds as a fallback to the live socket).

exec: pm.test('Marked as read, or none to mark', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 404]));

request.description:
**Access:** 🔑 Signed in (your own notifications)

Idempotent: marking an already-read notification keeps its original read time. Run *List notifications* first so `notification_id` holds a real UUID.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Marked as read |
| 404 | Not found, not yours, or not a UUID |

**Access:** 🔑 Signed in

Marks every unread notification of yours as read. `data.marked` is how many changed.

exec: pm.test('Authorized for your own channel', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json()).to.have.property('auth'); });

urlencoded.description: Assigned by Reverb when the socket connects; any value works for this check

request.description:
**Access:** 🔑 Signed in

The request Laravel Echo makes before it subscribes to a private channel. A user may join **only their own** channel, `private-App.Models.User.{their id}`. Run *Login* or *Current user* first so `user_id` is set.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | `{ "auth": "…" }` signature for your own channel |
| 403 | Someone else's channel; change `user_id` to try it |

item.name: 8. Webhooks
item.description:
Called by **Stripe**, never by the app. It is public (no bearer token) and secured by Stripe's **signature**, so a hand-made request from Postman is rejected.

To exercise it locally use the Stripe CLI:
```
stripe listen --forward-to localhost:8000/api/webhooks/stripe
stripe trigger checkout.session.completed
```
Put the `whsec_…` secret it prints into `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

header.description: Computed by Stripe. This placeholder will be rejected.

request.description:
**Access:** 🌐 Public, verified by Stripe's signature

The authoritative confirmation that a payment succeeded. It activates the subscription (the same idempotent action as *Confirm subscription*), so whichever arrives first wins and the other changes nothing.

This request exists to document the endpoint; with a fake signature it is **rejected**, which is the correct behavior.

item.name: 9. Developer tools (local only)
item.description:
🧪 **Only registered when `APP_ENV` is `local` or `testing`.** In production these return **404**. In Docker they are available only in **demo mode** (`.\scripts\setup.ps1 -Mode demo`). They exist so the certificate flow can be tested without watching every lesson.

They write lesson progress only; they **never** write learning-engagement data, because that drives revenue splits and instructor payouts. Student accounts only.

exec: pm.test('Tool ran (200) or is switched off (404 in production)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 404]));

request.description:
**Access:** 🧪 Local/demo, student token

Marks every lesson of the next `count` (1–5, default 2) published courses as completed for the signed-in student, then runs the real certificate flow. `generate_pdf: true` renders the PDF immediately, so no queue worker is needed. Courses that already have a certificate are skipped.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Processed; `data.courses` lists what happened |
| 403 | Not a student account |
| 404 | Production: the tool is switched off |

exec: pm.test('Reset (200) or switched off (404 in production)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 404]));

request.description:
**Access:** 🧪 Local/demo, student token

Deletes **your own** certificates (and their PDFs) and lesson progress so a test can be repeated. Other students are untouched.

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 200 | Cleared |
| 404 | Production: the tool is switched off |

item.name: 10. Operations
item.description: Infrastructure checks for the Docker deployment. Not part of the product API.

request.description:
**Access:** 🌐 Public

A cheap check served by nginx itself (it does not touch PHP or the database). It exists **only in the Docker image**; under Herd or `php artisan serve` it returns 404. For a deeper check use *List active plans*, which exercises PHP and the database.
